AIML Module Project - UnsupervisedLearning - Aaditya Kumar Ravi¶

Part A - 30 Marks¶

• DOMAIN: Automobile
• CONTEXT: The data concerns city-cycle fuel consumption in miles per gallon to be predicted in terms of 3 multivalued discrete and 5 continuous attributes.
• DATA DESCRIPTION: | | | |--|--|
|cylinders: multi-valued discrete|acceleration: continuous|
|displacement: continuous model|year: multi-valued discrete|
|horsepower: continuous|origin: multi-valued discrete|
|weight: continuous|car name: string (unique for each instance)|
|mpg: continuous| |

• PROJECT OBJECTIVE: To understand K-means Clustering by applying on the Car Dataset to segment the cars into various categories.
• STEPS AND TASK [30 Marks]:
1. Data Understanding & Exploration: [5 Marks]

3. Clustering: [15 Marks]¶
A. Apply K-Means clustering for 2 to 10 clusters. [3 Marks]¶
In [88]:
from scipy.stats import zscore

cardfattr = cardf.iloc[:, 1:9] #excluding first column car_name
cardfscaled = cardfattr.apply(zscore) #scaling the dataframe for excluded car_name column
cardfscaled.head() #view the scaled data

In [90]:
#import the required library
from sklearn.cluster import KMeans 
from sklearn.metrics import silhouette_samples, silhouette_score
In [91]:
wss=[] #within cluster sum of squares
for i in range(2,11):
    km = KMeans(n_clusters=i, n_init='auto') #initialize kmeans clustering
    km.fit(cardfscaled) #fit the kmeans clustering on scaled data
    wss.append(km.inertia_) #sum of squared distances of samples to their closest cluster center
    print("Silhouette Score for cluster", i, ":", silhouette_score(cardfscaled, km.labels_))

B. Plot a visual and find elbow point. [2 Marks]¶
In [92]:
plt.plot(range(2,11), wss, 'rx-')
Out[92]:
[<matplotlib.lines.Line2D at 0x1904481b050>]
  • it looks like elbow point is at cluster 5 because the rate of wss descrease is slow down at this pont and also the silhouette score is good, so the optimal number of clusters for this kMeans clustering is 5
C. On the above visual, highlight which are the possible Elbow points. [1 Marks]¶
  • Looking at the above visual, there are 3 points where graph bends like elbow
  • First at cluster=3 but this is not an optimal elbow point becuase the wss descrease is still high as it is dropping from 1200 to 800 when we find next elbow point at 5
  • Second at cluster=5 which looks like perfect elbow point because comparatively the wss decrease is slow now and silhouette score(0.33) is also better than cluster 3(0.32) and 8(0.28)
  • Third at cluster=8 which also doesn't look like perfect elbow point and the silhouette score(0.28) is also less than cluster 5(0.33).

Hence n_cluster=5 is the best elbow point.

D. Train a K-means clustering model once again on the optimal number of clusters. [3 Marks]¶
In [93]:
km_clusters = KMeans(n_clusters=5, n_init='auto') #initialize the kMeans clustering model
km_clusters.fit(cardfscaled) #train the model

Part B - 30 Marks¶

• DOMAIN: Automobile
• CONTEXT: The purpose is to classify a given silhouette as one of three types of vehicle, using a set of features extracted from the silhouette. The vehicle may be viewed from one of many different angles.
• DATA DESCRIPTION: The data contains features extracted from the silhouette of vehicles in different angles. Four "Corgie" model vehicles were used for the experiment: a double decker bus, Cheverolet van, Saab 9000 and an Opel Manta 400 cars. This particular combination of vehicles was chosen with the expectation that the bus, van and either one of the cars would be readily distinguishable, but it would be more difficult to distinguish between the cars.
• All the features are numeric i.e. geometric features extracted from the silhouette.
• PROJECT OBJECTIVE: Apply dimensionality reduction technique – PCA and train a model and compare relative results.
• STEPS AND TASK [30 Marks]:

1. Data Understanding & Cleaning: [5 Marks]¶

from sklearn import metrics

train_predclass = svcModel.predict(X_train) #test the model

print("Training Score:", svcModel.score(X_train, Y_train))
print("Testing Score:", svcModel.score(X_test, Y_test))

print("Train Recall Score:", metrics.recall_score(Y_train, train_predclass, average='macro'))

print("Train Precision Score:", metrics.precision_score(Y_train, train_predclass, average='macro')) 
print("Test Precision Score:", metrics.precision_score(Y_test, test_predclass, average='macro'))   
      
print("Train F1 Score:", metrics.f1_score(Y_train, train_predclass, average='macro'))
print("Test F1 Score:", metrics.f1_score(Y_test, test_predclass, average='macro')) 

print("Train Classification Report:\n", metrics.classification_report(Y_train, train_predclass))
print("Test Classification Report:\n", metrics.classification_report(Y_test, test_predclass))

5. Data Understanding & Cleaning: [5 Marks]¶
A. Explain pre-requisite/assumptions of PCA. [2 Marks]¶

PCA stands for Principal Component Analysis. PCA is an important method of feature extraction or say dimensionality reduction. It is taken into consideration when we have large number of features in the dataset and it is very difficult to visualize all those features in those many number of dimensions and it becomes very complex. So to overcome this issue, we use PCA technique.
But there are following pre-requisite/assumptions for doing PCA which we have also done in this project:

  • Data should be numerical in all features. PCA works best with numerical data. Categorical variables are typically not suitable for PCA without appropriate encoding or preprocessing.
  • PCA works best when the features are scaled to have comparable variances. Scaling ensures that features with larger variances do not dominate the principal components. we can do scaling using ZScore, StandardScaler or MinMaxScaler etc.
  • PCA assumes linear relationship between the underlying features in the dataset.
  • PCA assumes that the principal components or say the derived features are orthogonal i.e 90 degree to each other.
  • No missing values should be there for better results. we can impute the missing or unexpected values beforehand of applying PCA
B. Explain advantages and limitations of PCA. [3 Marks]¶

Advantages of PCA:

  • PCA reduces the number of features in the dataset, making it easier to visualize, store, and analyze. This can be especially beneficial for high-dimensional datasets with many features.
  • By reducing dimensions, PCA can help visualize high-dimensional data in fewer dimensions, making it easier to identify patterns and relationships.
  • PCA focuses on capturing the most significant variation in the data which reduces the noise and overfitting as well.
  • Models trained on PCA-reduced data is faster and be less computationally expensive becasue less data to process.

Limitations of PCA:

  • Reducing dimensions leads to some loss of information. While PCA tries to minimize this loss, it's important to be aware of what information might be discarded.
  • Data must be normalized/standardized before applying PCA
  • It is difficult to Interpret Principal Components. The new features created by PCA is linear combinations of the original features, making their interpretation less intuitive compared to the original features.
  • It is sensitive to scaling. Feature scaling can significantly impact the results of PCA. It's crucial to properly scale your data before applying PCA to avoid biased results.
  • PCA is not suitable for all data types. PCA works best with numerical data. It's not directly applicable to categorical or text data without additional transformations.
